small_guidance:
- Add a GROUP_M block-swizzle (e.g. 8) to both GEMM kernels for better L2 reuse across N tiles; the M=16384, N=4096/1024 shapes benefit significantly from row-group scheduling.
- Expand autotune configs with larger tiles (BLOCK_M=256, BLOCK_N=128, BLOCK_K=64, num_warps=8, num_stages=4) — the first GEMM is 16384×4096×2048 which is compute-bound and rewards bigger tiles; also try num_stages=4 for better K-loop pipelining.
- For the second GEMM (N=1024) fuse the logsumexp directly into the epilogue: each program tile holds a full row slice of size BLOCK_N; with BLOCK_N=1024 a single program per row can compute max and sum-exp in registers, eliminating the separate logsumexp kernel and the write/read of the 16384×1024 intermediate.
large_guidance:
- Fuse linear2 + logsumexp into one persistent kernel: since output_size=1024 fits comfortably in registers/SRAM, launch one program per row (or row-tile) that computes the full 1024-wide GEMV-style output, then performs the online (one-pass) max + sum-exp reduction in the epilogue without ever materializing the (16384,1024) tensor.
- Consider split-K or stream-K for the first GEMM (M=16384, N=4096, K=2048): K=2048 is large enough that splitting K across SMs and doing an atomic/partial-sum reduction may improve SM occupancy on the 4090.
- Store weight2 pre-transposed (K-contiguous along the inner dim) at init time so the fused linear2+logsumexp kernel can do fully coalesced loads without relying on strided B access; same for weight1 if the autotuned tile shapes prefer a particular layout.
